bottom_line: In patients with a myocardial infarction 1 to 3 years earlier, ticagrelor (90 mg or 60 mg twice daily) vs placebo reduced cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (hazard ratio 0.85 [95% CI, 0.75 to 0.96] for 90 mg; 0.84 [95% CI, 0.74 to 0.95] for 60 mg).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, ticagrelor 90 mg or 60 mg twice daily (on background aspirin) lowered the 3-year Kaplan–Meier rate of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (7.85% and 7.77% vs 9.04%; hazard ratios 0.85 and 0.84 with 95% CIs excluding 1.0), while increasing TIMI major bleeding (2.60% and 2.30% vs 1.06%; hazard ratios 2.69 and 2.32). The reported rates of fatal bleeding or nonfatal intracranial hemorrhage were <1% over 3 years in all groups, and death from any cause did not differ significantly by dose vs placebo (1.00 [0.86–1.16] and 0.89 [0.76–1.04]).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with three parallel groups (ticagrelor 90 mg, ticagrelor 60 mg, placebo) and background aspirin.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned, in a double-blind 1:1:1 fashion, 21,162 patients who had had a myocardial infarction 1 to 3 years earlier to ticagrelor at a dose of 90 mg twice daily, ticagrelor at a dose of 60 mg twice daily, or placebo.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke; primary safety end point was TIMI major bleeding.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke. The primary safety end point was Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) major bleeding.

major_points.text: TIMI major bleeding was higher with ticagrelor vs placebo, while intracranial hemorrhage or fatal bleeding rates were reported as similar across groups in the abstract.
major_points.quote: Rates of TIMI major bleeding were higher with ticagrelor (2.60% with 90 mg and 2.30% with 60 mg) than with placebo (1.06%) (P<0.001 for each dose vs. placebo); the rates of intracranial hemorrhage or fatal bleeding in the three groups were 0.63%, 0.71%, and 0.60%, respectively.

major_points.text: Premature discontinuation of treatment occurred more often in ticagrelor groups than placebo over the duration of the trial.
major_points.quote: The proportions of patients in each group who discontinued treatment prematurely over the duration of the trial were 32.0% in the group that received 90 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, 28.7% in the group that received 60 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, and 21.4% in the placebo group

major_points.text: Dyspnea occurred more frequently with ticagrelor and more often led to study-drug discontinuation than placebo.
major_points.quote: Dyspnea was more frequent with the two ticagrelor doses, with 3-year event rates of 18.93% in the group that received 90 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, 15.84% in the group that received 60 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, and 6.38% in the placebo group

absolute_effects.text: Kaplan–Meier rates at 3 years for TIMI major bleeding: 2.60% (ticagrelor 90 mg), 2.30% (ticagrelor 60 mg), 1.06% (placebo).
absolute_effects.quote: Kaplan–Meier rates at 3 years were 2.60% in the group that received 90 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, 2.30% in the group that received 60 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, and 1.06% in the placebo group

Dyspnea was more frequent with the two ti- cagrelor doses, with 3-year event rates of 18.93% in the group that received 90 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, 15.84% in the group that received 60 mg of ticagrelor twice daily, and 6.38% in the placebo group

absolute_effects.text: Fatal bleeding or nonfatal intracranial hemorrhage: 0.63% (ticagrelor 90 mg), 0.71% (ticagrelor 60 mg), 0.60% (placebo).

subgroups.text: Subgroups included age, sex, race, weight, type of index MI, time from MI to randomization, PCI history, diabetes, multivessel disease, chronic kidney disease, aspirin dose, and geographic region.
subgroups.quote: These subgroups included age, sex, race, weight, type of index myocardial infarction, time from qualifying myocardial infarc- tion to randomization, history of percutaneous coronary intervention

harms.text: TIMI major bleeding was higher with ticagrelor vs placebo with hazard ratios and CIs.
Dyspnea was more frequent with ticagrelor vs placebo with hazard ratios and CIs.
Dyspnea leading to study-drug discontinuation occurred more frequently with ticagrelor vs placebo.
Gout adverse events were more frequent with ticagrelor than placebo.

analysis_methods.text: Primary efficacy analysis was intention-to-treat, time-to-event from randomization to first primary composite event.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary efficacy analysis was conducted on an intention-to-treat basis, with each dose com- pared with placebo, as a time-to-event analysis from randomization to the first occurrence

analysis_methods.text: Estimated 1360 primary end-point events required; power targets for each ticagrelor dose comparison vs placebo stated.
analysis_methods.quote: We estimated that a total of 1360 primary end- point events would be required in order to pro- vide the study with approximately 90% power

analysis_methods.text: Haybittle–Peto approach used for interim analysis; final significance threshold stated.
analysis_methods.quote: a Haybittle– Peto approach was used to take into account an interim analysis of efficacy

analysis_methods.text: Hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals generated with Cox proportional-hazards model; two-sided P values.
analysis_methods.quote: Hazard ratios and 95% con- fidence intervals were generated with the use of a Cox proportional-hazards model, and all report- ed P values are two-sided.

analysis_methods.text: Alpha was apportioned to each ticagrelor dose comparison vs placebo to control overall type I error using correlation of 0.5.
analysis_methods.quote: To control the overall type I error, alpha was apportioned to the comparison of each ticagrelor dose with placebo (with the use of a correlation of 0.5 between the test statistics)

criticisms.text: Safety findings should not be generalized to populations at heightened bleeding risk because the protocol excluded patients with recent bleeding, prior stroke, or need for oral anticoagulant therapy.
criticisms.quote: Therefore, the safety profile of long-term ticagrelor that we observed should not be gener- alized to other populations at heightened risk for bleeding.
